chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Jamars (pillars of stone), so he said: 'Stand at the two Jamars and do not stand at Jamarat al-Aqabah.' I said: 'Is this from the Sunnah?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'What should I say when I throw?' He said: 'Say Allahu Akbar with each pebble.'

key_terms.السُّنَّةِ: The Sunnah, referring to the prophetic tradition or established practice of the Imams.
key_terms.الْجِمَارِ: The Jamars, plural of Jamarah, referring to the pillars or stone markers used in the ritual of Rami al-Jamarat.
key_terms.جَمْرَةِ الْعَقَبَةِ: Jamarat al-Aqabah, the largest and final Jamarah in Mina, where pilgrims throw seven pebbles.
key_terms.حَصَاةٍ: A pebble or small stone used for the ritual throwing.
key_terms.كَبِّرْ: Say 'Allahu Akbar' (God is the Greatest), the specific dhikr prescribed for the act of throwing.

ai.seo_question: What is the correct method and recitation for throwing pebbles at the Jamars during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Sunnah of standing position during the Rami al-Jamarat, distinguishing between the three Jamars by instructing pilgrims to remain stationary at the first two while moving to the third. It further establishes the ritual etiquette of uttering 'Allahu Akbar' with each pebble, linking the physical act of casting stones to the spiritual remembrance of God, a practice deeply rooted in Shia fiqh regarding the Hajj rituals.
